purpose: Test whether RECE's existing preservation mechanism (retain_texts) prevents historical-prompt (English springer) corruption when applied AT Stage 1, before the damage occurs, on S2 (English springer -> golf ball) -- the reverse-sequence question explicitly left open by stage1_history_intervention (S1). Existing-method control, not a new method.

parent.note: untouched author parent (M0 -> English springer), same as S2's parent; NEVER build from S2_Stage1 or any refined checkpoint

comparator: existing S2_Stage1 (blank preservation), sha256 76c8740e543b90b5b065aceb7bb7772f186b9f3a9fd38f81d4d16b1c6d3895ee -- images, labels, predictions reused unmodified, not regenerated

reused_panel.design: 20 cases each: golf ball, English springer, French horn, parachute -- identical manifest, not reconstructed or rewritten

execution_order: 1. Verify parent hash, S2_Stage1 comparator hash, manifest hash, pinned-source checks.
2. Build S2_STAGE1_HISTORY from the untouched parent (GPU, native fp32 Stage-1 edit only).
3. Verify exactly 32 changed keys, 654 unchanged, all finite, exact reload.
4. Generate 80 images on the reused manifest; release GPU.

5. Individually review all 40 target-role images (golf ball 0-19 new target, English springer 60-79 historical target) at native 512px; grid-review the 2 retained classes (parachute 20-39, French horn 40-59), escalating on uncertainty.
6. Freeze and hash labels before classification.
8. Compute joint outcomes against S2_Stage1, EnglishSpringer_parent, and M0.
tolerances: native fp32 Stage-1 verification only (exact key-set/reload checks); the fp64 reference solver's 1e-10 backward-error tolerance does NOT apply here and is not imposed
scoped_stop_rule: on a consequential provenance or source-drift failure, stop and preserve evidence; narrow runtime fixes that leave scientific settings unchanged are allowed
forbidden: automatic advance to refinement even if Stage 1 improves
